entries.title: Verify localizes failures, gates Merriam once, and Publish never runs on a dirty tree
entries.brief: Cards verify with the integration tests and repo scans they touch; the plan verify runs once as a gate on Merriam, which fixes a failure in a fork and waits on forks instead of polling; Publish never verifies or pushes a dirty tree; verify is never skipped after a crash; every agent prompt goes through a file
entries.body:
## Goal

A failing integration test stops on the card that caused it, Publish never verifies or pushes a dirty tree, and no gate is skipped after a crash.
refusal-audit stopped five times on integration-verify regressions that the plan-level verify could not localize.
Webster's plan verify runs once, as a gate on Merriam that sends a failure back to Merriam to fix, and Merriam waits on its forks instead of polling (`webster-verify-gate` below).

## Also folded in, not in bolt before

- refusal-audit self-report 2: card `verify:` commands run package-scoped, so `cmd/lyx` repo-wide invariant scans first run at the plan level; Plan-Write could append `go test ./cmd/lyx/`.
- refusal-audit self-report 3: Webster's integration verify runs against the working tree, so an uncommitted edit can mask a non-compiling HEAD.
- Publish's conflict resolver reuses `.lyx/loom/conflict-resolution-r1.md` across Publishes (`internal/mergeresolve/spec.go:60`), so a later conflicting merge-in is refused while an earlier file exists; refusal-audit hit it.
- Deliver every agent prompt through a file, so no role can hit the 30000-byte launch limit (`internal/shuttleengine/claudeengine/command.go`); Master already does (`e39909bbc`).

## From `card-verify-integration`: Cards that touch integration-tagged tests verify with -tags integration

No refusal-audit card declared a verify: line; the fork gate is go build plus the package's unit tests (webster-body-implementer.md:30), untagged, while 11 of 48 touched test files are //go:build integration.
Want: Plan-Write adds `go test -tags integration <pkg>` to a card's verify when it touches a tagged file; a message-rewording card greps the repo for the old text first so stale exact-string assertions become part of the card; Master re-runs integration tests after a rework fork.

## From `publish-dirty-tree`: Publish must not verify or push a dirty tree after merge resolution

refusal-audit's Publish merge left historyfold_test.go uncommitted and verify ran on the dirty tree; earlier publish-review-fixback had the same uncommitted merge-resolution edits

## From `verify-gate-crash-after-merge`: Landing verify gate skips a merge interrupted before its marker write

Found reviewing PR #308 (`publish-verify-after-merge`).
Fabric reports a finished-but-interrupted merge as already up to date, so the gate cannot tell a verified tree from an unverified one.
Robust fix: record the task HEAD that last passed verify, and verify whenever HEAD differs from it.

## From `webster-verify-gate`: verify is a gate on Merriam, Merriam waits instead of polling, and its strand is named webster

A webster run's integration tests run once per attempt, as a mechanical gate on Merriam, and a failure goes back to Merriam to fix; Merriam waits on its forks instead of polling.
Merriam's strand is named for what it is.

### Today

- Merriam's stencil (`contracts/stencils/webster/webster-template-master.md`) spawns an integration fork that runs the plan's `## verify:` once and writes `OK | FAILED`; on `FAILED` Merriam fixes nothing and stops.
- After Merriam exits, Go runs the same `## verify:` again, with no strand and an empty `activity.wait`, so the suite runs twice and the second run is invisible.
- `webster-recovery` (D5/D6, landed `3c791470d`) added one fix attempt by a separate session at run exit, with the bisected card as a hint; on its first run the bisect named card 07 for a line card 09 wrote.
- Merriam polls `lyx webster await-batch` in the foreground every ~30s for as long as a fork runs, and polls the integration report with `sleep 20; test -f`.
  The stencil says a backgrounded wait ends the turn and kills the run; that predates shuttle's `EventWaiting` (`internal/shuttleengine/claudeengine/background.go`), which reads a turn end with a running background fork as still running.
- Merriam's strand shows as `<shortname>:<slug>:master`: webster spawns it with `string(RoleMaster)` (`internal/websterengine/runlevel.go`), the same value that keys its model in `webster.yaml`.
### Fix direction

- Merriam's strand gets a shuttle gate (`shuttleengine.GateOutcome`, as Discussion-Write and Burler use) that runs the plan's `## verify:` when Merriam reports done.
  A failing gate injects its findings into Merriam's session; Merriam forks a fixer with the full plan context, and the gate re-runs, up to an attempt cap Discussion sets.
- The gate is the only run of the suite: Merriam's integration fork and Go's separate post-exit verify go.
- This replaces `webster-recovery`'s D5/D6 recovery session; Discussion finds why the bisect named the wrong card and decides whether it survives as a hint in the gate's findings.
- While the gate runs, `activity.wait` names it.
- Merriam spawns each fork in the background, ends its turn, and acts on the fork's completion notification; the stencil's polling and its "started non-interactively" framing go.
  Discussion confirms Merriam's strand is waited on through the shuttle loop that reads `EventWaiting`.
- Discussion measures whether a re-run after a fix hits Go's test cache, and if the integration tests defeat it, re-runs the failed packages before the full suite.
- Merriam's strand gets the role `webster`, separate from its model key; whether the `master` model key in `webster.yaml` is renamed too is for Discussion, and a rename must keep existing configs loading.
### Done when

- A webster run runs the plan's `## verify:` once per gate attempt, visible in `activity`.
- A regression introduced by a card goes back to Merriam and is fixed in the same run, pinned by a test.
- Merriam's stencil contains no polling loop, and a batch completes with Merriam idle between the fork spawn and its notification.
- A webster run's Merriam strand is named `<shortname>:<slug>:webster`.
- The webster module doc and `docs/overview.md` describe the gate, and CLAUDE.md's Merriam terminology entry stays accurate.


## Landed on main ahead of this task (2026-10-03)

- Merriam waits on its forks' completion notifications instead of polling (`9ae921b24`): the stencil's polling loops are gone, and `await-batch` stays only as an operator verb. The verify gate, the strand rename and the rest of `webster-verify-gate` remain here.
- `begin-batch`'s model assertion is dormant, not a cost: `run` baselines `AssertedModel` to Merriam's launch model, so the check is a string comparison that never injects. Removing it touches state, docs and a sandbox scenario for no runtime gain; Discussion decides whether it goes.

entries.title: Clean pair lifecycle: no leftover sessions, branches, sockets or races
entries.brief: fabric remove ends the pair's tmux session, finishes half-removed pairs and deletes warp branches on origin; loom start never races a dying driver
entries.body:
## Goal

Removing a pair ends its tmux session first, can finish a half-removed pair, and leaves no branches or stray directories behind; starting a run never races a dying driver.

## Also folded in, not in bolt before

- After refusal-audit landed, the driver wrote a drive report into the weft; `lyx fabric remove --remote` removed the task worktree, refused the dirty weft, and a rerun answered "worktree not found", so the half-removed pair had to be finished by hand.
- Warp branches on origin (see `fabric-branch-hygiene` below): `remove --remote` deletes the weft branch on origin but never the warp branch, and squash merges mean git never sees them as merged.
  On 2026-10-02 the hub deleted 37 such warp branches by hand (no open PR, no live pair).
  Want: `remove --remote` deletes the warp branch on origin too, and `fabric cleanup --remote` finds warp branches on origin with no live pair and no open PR.

## From `fabric-remove-ends-reed-session`: fabric remove leaves the pair tmux session alive

Seen 2026-09-30 for quarry-cli-answers and status-strand-by-driver: after landing and `fabric remove --remote`, their reed sessions were still alive hours later.
A driver that wrote its stop report after the removal recreated `<hub>/<slug>/.lyx/...` and `<hub>/<slug>/_lyx/shed/<slug>/drive-reports/<report>.md`: a stray directory, and a drive report that never reached the archive.
The hub killed the sessions and deleted the dirs by hand.

Fix: remove (and batten teardown) ends the pair reed session (reed down) before deleting the worktrees, and waits for or refuses on a live driver; a stop report written after done should land before the archive tag.

## From `driver-restart-race`: loom start races the ly-drive self-removal and ends with no driver

After a hand-back, the ly-drive session removes its own strand with a detached `lyx reed remove --name loom-driver --detach` that waits for the session's pid to exit (end-of-session command from `083e992cf`).
A `lyx loom start` issued in that window sees the loom-driver strand still live, keeps it instead of spawning a driver, and the detached remover then deletes it: the run is left with no driver and nothing happens (hit on `batten-hub-ready` and `focus-marker-warn`, 2026-09-30; a second `loom start` works).
Fix direction: `loom start` treats a driver strand with a pending self-removal (or whose claude has exited) as gone and spawns a fresh one, or the remover skips a strand that was re-adopted since it was scheduled.

## From `fabric-branch-hygiene`: Fabric: branches left behind by a failed add and on the remote

Read the closed GitHub issues #269 (add rollback leaves the warp branch) and #270 (cleanup cannot see weft branches stranded on the remote). Re-check both once `landing` has landed: it takes #293 (remove leaves the warp branch, locally and on origin), which touches the same branch-lifecycle code, and the ly-drive may repair the rest from a trace.

After `landing` (#298): `fabric remove` now deletes the local warp branch, but `--remote` still deletes only the weft branch on origin; warp branches of removed pairs stay there (`board-done-on-landing`, `burler-exclude-warn`, `integration-verify-fence`, `loom-start-layout`, `stencil-drift-remedy`, `stuck-reason-in-status`, `landing`). Out of scope in landing's decision record.

## From `main-weft-not-pushed`: main-weft is never pushed and never advances on landing

Seen 2026-09-30, uninvestigated: the prime weft branch main-weft stays local and does not move when a task lands

entries.title: PATTERN for loomyard, manifest/ retired, plus repo conventions
entries.brief: CONSTRAINTS.md becomes _lyx/PATTERN.md so agents get the constraints directive; manifest/ retires into bolt and package docs; warp/weft scan beyond Go code; model specs in short form; role constants; ide workspace cleanups
entries.body:
## Goal

loomyard gets `_lyx/PATTERN.md` so lyx agents receive the constraints directive, which no run has received so far; CONSTRAINTS.md moves there.
`manifest/` is retired in the same pass, since both sweeps repoint the same docs, stencils and CLAUDE.md.
Runs alone, last: it repoints CONSTRAINTS.md in ~130 files.

## Also folded in

- `fabric-vocabulary-everywhere`, `model-spec-short-form`, `ide-hub-workspace-followups`, `agent-role-constants` and `manifest-retire` below.
- `manifest-retire`'s Someday strike list needs the operator before this task starts.
- `model-spec-short-form`'s model trial (`fable[high]` for discussion and review) moved to `convergence-plan`, where it is measured; this task does only the short form, the dead link and Master's explicit effort.

## From `pattern-init`: Initialize PATTERN for loomyard: CONSTRAINTS.md becomes _lyx/PATTERN.md

Operator 2026-10-01: CONSTRAINTS.md is millhouse's setup; loomyard's variant is PATTERN, not yet initialized.
Verified: no _lyx/PATTERN.md in loomyard-weft, and there is no init verb. internal/pattern injects a role directive (implementer, review-fix, orchestrator) pointing at _lyx/PATTERN.md into webster fork/Master, burler and loom plan prompts only when the file exists, so today's runs got no PATTERN directive (they only saw CONSTRAINTS.md through CLAUDE.md and stencil mentions).
Work: move CONSTRAINTS.md's invariants into _lyx/PATTERN.md (weft, invisible to the code repo; optionally split under _lyx/pattern/); repoint everything that names CONSTRAINTS.md: CLAUDE.md, stencils (loom discussion/plan/rework, webster master and prefix-recovery), the ly-drive skill, contracts/specs, burlercli/run.go, loomshed and treadleengine docs, and contracts/stencils/citation_enforcement_test.go; decide whether a `lyx pattern init` verb is wanted for other repos.

## From `fabric-vocabulary-everywhere`: Fabric vocabulary: warp and weft only inside fabric, also in docs, specs and tests

Operator 2026-09-30: warp and weft are fabric-internal words; nothing outside fabric should know them.
Seen on refusal-audit: contracts/specs/refusal-spec.md and several _test.go files outside fabric use them, and the scan let them through.
Want: extend the scan to contracts/, docs/, manifest/, plugins/ skills and test files outside the owner set (or an explicit allowlist for fabric docs), and sweep the existing hits.

## From `model-spec-short-form`: Model specs in the short form everywhere, and per-role model choice revisited

Seen 2026-10-01: long form in internal/loomengine/template.yaml (discussion, plan, review, friction), internal/websterengine/template.yaml (recovery), internal/landingshed/template.yaml (conflict, describe) and contracts/specs/llm-model-spec.md's examples; the spec only mentions in one sentence that a bare bracket token means effort. Template comments cite docs/reference/model-spec.md, which is missing; the spec lives at contracts/specs/llm-model-spec.md.
Webster master is plain `sonnet`, so its effort (medium) comes invisibly from models.yaml; write it explicitly.
Model choice (operator, 2026-10-01): try `fable[high]` for discussion and review, where design judgement matters (refusal-audit's holes came from opus Discussion and opus reviews; a Fable review found the design problem), keep sonnet for implementation; change it only between runs and measure review rounds, PR rejects and interventions before and after (convergence-plan).

## From `ide-hub-workspace-followups`: ide hub workspace: review follow-ups

Follow-ups from the PR #301 review (`85902381e`), all non-blocking:
- `internal/fabricengine/hubworkspace.go` builds the prime path by hand (`filepath.Join(l.HubPath, primeName, l.AnchorRel)`) instead of `WorktreePath`.
- `internal/ideengine/spawn.go` now WARNs on every spawn whose prime resolution fails, task spawns included (silent before).
- Removing the last pair prunes `_portals/<anchor>`, so the hub workspace shows a missing folder until the next prime spawn.
- Relative-path settings spliced from the prime into the workspace file resolve against `_launchers/`, not the prime.

## From `agent-role-constants`: each module names the agents it spawns with its own constant

Operator 2026-10-02: role names stay owned by the module that spawns the agent; no central list, since a new module with its own agent must touch no shared file, and `agentname`'s role set stays open.
Seen: most spawn sites pass their role as an inline literal (`driver` in `loomcli/driverspec.go`, `discussion`/`plan`/`rework` in `loomengine`, `burler`, `friction`, `describe`, `conflict`, `judge`/`triage`/`targeting` in `treadleengine`).
Want: each spawn site takes its role from a named constant in its own module, and the Agent Name Invariant states that the spawning module owns its role.
Webster's own `master` → `webster` rename is in `webster-verify-gate`.


## From `manifest-retire`: retire manifest/ into bolt and package docs

Retire `manifest/`: first bring roadmap.md's surviving Someday items into bolt in the new tier format, then move the durable reference content into package docs, fix inbound links and delete the folder.
Millhouse has no ownership of `manifest/` (operator, 2026-10-02).

### Someday items still to triage with the operator

Not yet in bolt: `raddle`, `hardener`, `webster-parallel-execution`, `reed-multi-window`, `warp-visibility`, `baseline-drift-gate`, `config-overlay`, `fabric-reset-to-sha`, `finalize-discrepancy-doc`, `shedrecipe-capabilities`, `doctor`, `session-sync`.
Proposed strikes, awaiting the operator: fabric Windows verification (dropping Windows and CLAUDE.md's fslink claim), `semantic-index`, curation-triage automation, VS Code opt-in per worktree (check `batten-open-ide` first), plugin packaging, the shuttle tools-restriction and per-round provider selector, bulk-mode clusters, fabric's ordinary-monorepo verbs, the reed Slack relay.
### manifest/ retirement

The triage was done in the bolt review of 2026-10-01/02; what survives is already in bolt.
This task moves the durable reference content into package docs, fixes inbound links and deletes the folder (Millhouse has no ownership of `manifest/`).

- `manifest/HANDOFF.md`: the hub run loop goes to the `internal/orchcli` package doc; the rest is spent.
- `hardener.md`: the text-review vs behaviour-review distinction and the respawn rationale go to `internal/treadleengine`'s doc.
- `fabric-windows-verification.md`: the Linux-only caveat goes to the `internal/fabricengine` and `internal/fslink` docs.
- `webster-parallel-execution.md`: the 42-card case study and the index-race rationale go to `internal/websterengine`'s doc.
- `review-finding-classification.md`: the convergence case study goes to `internal/burlerengine`'s doc.
- `curation-triage.md`: one line in the boardengine doc ("anyone adds notes, the orchestrator curates"); the automation is struck.
- Inbound links: `internal/treadleengine/doc.go`, `internal/fabricengine/livestate_doc_test.go`, `contracts/specs/loom-plan-spec.md`, `docs/overview.md` (lifecycle text and design links), `crucible/README.md`, `crucible/review-prompt-template.md`, CLAUDE.md's Task completion rule, `.claude/agents/mill-done-gate-fixer.md`.


### From `manifest-to-bolt`: Move everything in manifest/ into bolt and retire the folder

Operator 2026-10-01: LYXHUB takes over all development of loomyard; everything in manifest/ goes into bolt.
The operator also says much of it is outdated: triage each roadmap Someday item with the operator (keep as tier 3 or tier 2, merge, or strike) and carry its designs/<name>.md over as the bolt entry's design doc.
Afterwards: delete manifest/, and update CLAUDE.md (Task completion section names manifest/roadmap.md and manifest/designs/), docs/overview.md's Documentation Lifecycle and any stencil or test that names manifest/.


## From `run-parentage`'s PR-Gate (2026-10-02): retire `seed.Parent`

`shedrun.Seed.Parent` is no longer written; parent comes from the pair's origin record, and the field is read only as a fallback for runs seeded before `aa67fd1d7`.
Remove the field and the fallback once no such run remains.

entries.title: Review convergence: the judge decides converged, continue or circling from fresh reviews
entries.brief: The Bouncer judge stops reviewing the artifacts and judges convergence from facts Go hands it (counts, severities, trend, reopened ledger keys), on its own sonnet[medium] key; at least one fresh round, circling escalates; plus finding classes
entries.body:
## Goal

A review segment stops when it has converged, judged from fresh reviews, and escalates when it circles.
Today the Bouncer judge is a second reviewer: `contracts/stencils/bouncer/bouncer-template-judge.md` opens with "You are a review-gate judge: a reviewer of the target artifacts against the rubric", reads the artifacts first, and `internal/shedadapters/bouncer.go` maps its APPROVED straight to Done.
So "every finding fixed" counts as converged, although the fixes are new text no fresh reviewer has seen.
The prompt is wrong by design, not the agent: it does what it is told (operator, 2026-10-02).

## Seen in rework-generations (2026-10-02)

One Discussion-Burler round found four MEDIUM, two LOW and two NIT; the fixer fixed all eight, three of them new design decisions; the judge checked each fix against the decision record, marked all resolved, and the segment ended without a second fresh review.
With a high-temperature reviewer every round is a new sample, and one sample cannot show convergence.

## Shape

- The judge's role is the operator's: a quick sit-rep agent that decides converged, continue or circling, and does not itself read the artifacts or the code.
- The judge decides all three outcomes; a pure mechanical rule was considered and rejected (operator, 2026-10-02): severities are the reviewer's own noisy labels, a nitpicky MEDIUM would force rounds up to `max_bounces`, and a reworded old finding looks new.
- Go hands the judge the facts instead of the artifacts: per round, the finding count and highest severity (and class, once findings carry one), the trend across rounds, and which ledger keys were reopened.
- Only two things stay mechanical: at least one fresh Burler round before convergence is possible (the seed entry has no fresh review, so it never converges straight away), and `max_bounces` as the upper bound.
- Fixed findings never count as convergence on their own; the fixes are new text, and the judge weighs whether the latest fresh review still found MEDIUM-or-worse.
- Circling escalates to the operator.
- The judge gets its own model key: today it shares loom's `review` key (`opus[effort=high]` in `internal/loomengine/template.yaml`) with the reviewers, which is part of why it acts as one; `judge: sonnet[medium]` (operator: Sonnet 5.5 is fast and cheap now, and the job is narrow).
- Applies to all three review segments (Discussion-, Plan- and Webster-Review).
- The reviewer's own top verdict (`verdict: APPROVED` with MEDIUM findings) mixes "not blocking" with "converged"; the judge must not read it as converged.
## Finding classes (from manifest/designs/review-finding-classification.md)

- Add a finding-class field (`design`, `scope`, `decision`, `consistency`) to burler's review contract and the rubrics; `internal/burlerengine/verdict.go` has only severity today.
- End the round loop when a round returns zero gating-class findings, keeping the cap as a backstop.
- Emit per-class counts in the round record, so the same class recurring across rounds is visible.
- Add a line to the Review Round Invariant: class decides who decides and when the loop stops, never whether a finding is fixed.

entries.title: Prompt-cache TTL per agent role
entries.brief: Parked: workers on 5m cache TTL, waiting sessions on 1h — operator deciding
entries.body:
Claude Code gives a subscription's main session a 1-hour prompt-cache TTL (cache write 2× base input) and subagents/forks 5 minutes (1.25×); every lyx agent is a main session in tmux, so all of them write at the 1-hour price (see https://code.claude.com/docs/en/prompt-caching.md).

Measured on the `landing` run's transcripts: Discussion, Plan, Bouncer and Burler never paused more than 90 s between turns, so 5 minutes keeps them warm; ly-drive paused up to 508 s (three gaps over 5 minutes), so it needs 1 hour. Webster Master waits on forks via Monitor and is not yet measured.

Likely shape: shuttle sets `CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL=5m|1h` (Claude Code v2.1.242+) per role when it spawns a session, configurable per role. loomyard was developed with the 5-minute limit in mind, so 5 minutes matches its design assumption.

entries.title: Convergence: measure hub and driver interventions, fix at the source, hardening freezes
entries.brief: Plan for lyx to converge rather than accumulate bugs: per-run intervention log, real-wiring tests, feature freezes
entries.body:
Operator 2026-09-30: take a step back and plan for convergence, not keep accepting more bugs.
Observed today: nearly every hub intervention was in same-day new code (#319: approve nil dep, reject reading its file argument as run-id), and both passed tests built on fake deps.
Ingredients: (1) log every hub intervention and ly-drive repair per run with a class and cause, so interventions per run and new-vs-repeat failure classes are visible; (2) every fix at the source with a test that drives the real CLI wiring, not only fakes; (3) freeze periods with no new verbs or recipe rows, hardening only, until the intervention rate flattens.
Goal: the outside LLM steps in rarely, and for the task rather than for lyx.
## Model trial (from `model-spec-short-form`, operator 2026-10-01)

Try `fable[high]` for discussion and review, where design judgement matters (refusal-audit's holes came from opus Discussion and opus reviews; a Fable review found the design problem), and keep sonnet for implementation.
Change it only between runs, and measure review rounds, PR rejects and interventions before and after.

## Friction on halt (from the hub, 2026-10-02)

A refusal or halt makes a friction note mandatory, so every intervention leaves a record the measurement can count.
Check first whether `internal/loomengine/anomaly.go` loses a halt that is later resumed.

entries.title: An MCP server over lyx exposing the verbs agents need
entries.brief: A few coarse MCP tools over lyx, chosen by measured agent use and exposed per role, so agents see typed schemas instead of guessing CLI shapes
entries.body:
## Why

Agents misuse or bypass lyx (the hub read `_board/*.json` with jq) because the CLI shape is not discoverable.
An MCP tool carries a typed input schema and a description.

## Constraint from the operator (2026-10-01)

Not one tool per verb: MCP entries are heavy.
Only the important ones are exposed, and how to pick them is still open.

## Proposed selection

1. **Measure first.** Mine transcripts and logs for which lyx commands agents run, where they fail, and where they read around lyx.
2. **Few coarse tools.** One tool per area with an `action` enum (the pattern of Claude Code's Artifact tool), e.g. `board`, `run` (status, approve, reject), `webster` (Master only); a handful in total.
3. **Per-role exposure.** A fork may get none, Master gets `webster`, the hub gets `board` and `run`.

## Shape

- A thin server shipped in the ly plugin; each action calls the same module seam the CLI uses, so behaviour never forks.
- The CLI stays for humans and scripts.
- Wins: no shell-quoted JSON payloads, and per-tool permissions (an agent can be denied `accept-audit`).

Related: `bolt-roadmap-tiers`, `process-naming`.


## Status: needs a careful design session first

Operator 2026-10-01: what goes into the MCP must be thought through very carefully; this is not a loom task yet.
Questions for that session:

- Which verbs need an MCP tool at all, and which are served well enough by a better `--help` (payload schema and an example per command) and a per-role command card in each stencil, generated from the cobra tree?
- Is permission gating (an agent denied `accept-audit` or `approve`) the real reason for MCP, since `--help` and cards cannot give it?
- One tool per module was raised and judged too heavy (long descriptions); what is the cut instead?

entries.title: creel: a mailbox between named lyx processes
entries.brief: Mail store and verbs on top of agent-naming's names; deferred while Claude's own SendMessage is enough
entries.body:
The mail store and verbs from `manifest/designs/reed-mailbox.md` (send, inbox, read, log; the watchdog delivering at idle; `inject` for privileged senders), addressed by `agent-naming`'s names.

Deferred (operator, 2026-10-02): Claude Code's own SendMessage is enough for now.
The address grammar in reed-mailbox.md (`name@slug[.hub]`) is superseded by `agent-naming`'s `<repo>:<slug>:<role>`, and its naming half moved into that task.
The design doc goes with `manifest/` in `bolt-v2`; this note keeps what is left of it.

Layering (operator, 2026-10-03): only reed talks to tmux, so the keystroke delivery is reed's: `reedengine.Engine.SendText`/`SendKey` exist, and a `lyx reed send <strand> <text>` verb exposes them; creel's `send`/`inject` deliver through it and never touch tmux themselves.
Use case: the operator's backup session on Remote Control rescues the orch, for example by re-enabling Remote Control after a cycle, and today has to find reed's per-hub tmux socket by hand; `lyx reed send ly:orch ...` covers it.

entries.title: One-screen overview of every run in the hub, in its own tmux window
entries.brief: One line per run with state, producer and age, instead of polling each run, shown without squeezing the orch pane (likely reed own-window anchoring)
entries.body:
From `manifest/HANDOFF.md`: one screen listing every run in the hub, one line each with state, producer and age.
`lyx shed status [run-id]` is per run and `lyx orch status` covers only the orchestrator, so the hub today polls each run separately.


## Where it shows


- Operator 2026-10-02: a status strand under orch would need its height to follow the number of runs, which reed cannot do; an own tmux window may fit better.
- reed today lays out one strand per pane in one window per worktree; `manifest/designs/reed-multi-window.md` sketches own-window strand anchoring, independent per-window attach via tmux session groups, and cross-worktree columns.
- Deep enough to stand alone, separate from `orch-owns-the-loop`.

entries.title: Discussion advisor: a dedicated agent answers Discussion-Write's questions live
entries.brief: A second agent spawned beside Discussion-Write studies the task and code and answers its design questions as they arise, a real two-agent dialogue
entries.body:
- **ask mode**: Discussion-Write asks its design questions as they arise, and an answerer replies; answers to design questions, not a review.
- **The answerer is a dedicated agent**, spawned in parallel with Discussion-Write with its own prompt: it studies the task, bolt and the code while the writer drafts, so it is ready when the questions come.
  It is an address, not hard-wired to `$LYX_PARENT`; the parent is the fallback.
- Two live sessions both keep their context, so this is a real dialogue, and none of it lands in the parent's context.
  Two agents designing together beat one agent asking and answering itself.
- `ask` and `review` are independent switches: an advisor answering interview questions and the parent reviewing the draft can both run on one task.
- New machinery: one producer running two interactive sessions side by side (e.g. `ly:<slug>:discussion` and `ly:<slug>:advisor`), each waiting on the other through files; shuttle keeps an asking session non-terminal today (`internal/shuttleengine/wait.go`), which is the starting point.

entries.title: Plan cards name the members they change as glyphs, after lyx's use of glyphs is tested systematically
entries.brief: Plan-Write lists file paths instead of member glyphs because its stencil shows and allows it, and handle-unreferenced forces invented glyphs; test lyx's use of quarry glyphs systematically first
entries.body:
## Why

Seen on `gate-list`'s plan (2026-10-02): card 1's `Edit:` lists 24 file paths and no member glyph, although its Intent names the members it changes (`GateSpec`, `GateOutcome`, `Run.evaluateGate`, `resolveGateSpec`, `burlerengine#Engine.Run`).
Webster's changed-files guard then compares at file level only, no `quarry resolve` confirms the members exist, and a kick-start pack (`kick-start-pack`) has no spans to pre-resolve.

## Causes, in `contracts/stencils/loom/loom-template-plan.md`

- The only card skeleton shows `**Edit:**` with `` - `path/to/file.go` ``, and agents copy the shape they are shown.
- The glyph rule says a *symbol* target is spelled as a glyph and "a file path stays a plain path"; nothing says an `Edit` target should be the members changed, so a file path is always a legal choice.
- File paths are the path of least resistance: a member glyph must be looked up with `lyx quarry` and resolve at validation, and can fail as `glyph-not-found`, `glyph-ambiguous` or `containment-unit-overlap`; a file path only has to exist.
- `handle-unreferenced` requires every `plan:` handle to be used by a later card, so a new symbol only its own card uses cannot take a handle; the planner then invents a glyph (`internal/shuttleengine#GateEntry` under `Create:`), which the handle rule exists to prevent.

## Want

- The skeleton and the text say `Edit:` lists the member glyphs changed; a file path only for a file with no symbol to name (tests, non-Go files).
- The plan rubric flags an `Edit` card holding only file paths while its Intent names specific symbols.
- `handle-unreferenced` does not fire for a handle its own declaring card uses.

## First: test loomyard's use of glyphs systematically (operator, 2026-10-02, refined 2026-10-03)

The glyph library is part of quarry and the operator has tested it hard; what has failed is loomyard's own use of it (the plan stencil, the handle rules and the containment checks, in the sections below).
Before the stencil change pushes every plan onto member glyphs, test that use systematically against real plans: resolve every member glyph a sample of real cards would name, the handle bind path and the containment checks, and record what fails.

## Validation must not change verdict mid-run (2026-10-02)

Seen on `rework-generations`, batch 5: a plan valid at Plan-Write was refused at `begin-batch` with `containment-file-overlap`.
Card 4 creates `loomshed#ReworkTold` with a `plan:` handle; card 5 lists both `internal/loomshed/prrework.go` and `loomshed#ReworkTold`; card 9 lists `prrework.go`.
While the unit did not exist the handle had no location, so containment could not place it; once card 4 built it and `begin-batch` canonicalized the handle into a glyph, containment saw the overlap for the first time.
Cards 5 and 9 sit in different, sequential batches, so the overlap was harmless; the member line in card 5 was redundant beside its own file line.

Want: validation gives the same answer at Plan-Write and at dispatch.
Either containment places a `plan:` handle by its declared file at plan time, or it does not refuse overlaps between cards in different batches; and a card listing a file and a member of that same file is flagged at plan time as redundant.

## Mechanical caller coverage for deletions (seen 2026-10-03)

In `test-suite-change-amplification`'s plan the Burler found cards 36, 37 and 39 deleting helpers whose callers sit in files the cards do not list; plan-validate could not see it, because a card lists files, not the symbols it deletes or re-signs.
Once cards name deleted and re-signed members as glyphs, plan-validate can resolve every reference through quarry and flag a referencing file that no card in the same or an earlier batch edits, instead of leaving it to the Burler or to verify's compile failure.

entries.title: Orch owns the run loop: detached batten start, a lyx watch, one land command, --continue, a committed role prompt
entries.brief: Replace the hub scratch scripts and remembered procedure with lyx itself, so an orch session runs the loop from its committed role prompt alone and resumes after a reboot
entries.body:
## Goal

An orch session runs the whole loop (start, watch, review, land, deploy) with lyx commands and its committed role prompt.
It needs no scripts in `.scratch/hub/` and no rules it must remember to read.

## Start a run detached

`lyx batten run <slug>` blocks in the foreground, so the orch backgrounds it from its own shell, and a Claude Code background job is killed at its time limit along with its process group: on 2026-10-02 all three batten runs died that way after 30 minutes.
The hub now starts them with `setsid nohup` by hand.
`lyx batten start <slug>` detaches batten's Go driver itself (`proc.Detach`, as `lyx loom start` does for loom's go driver).
How the operator sees many batten runs at once (a status strand, its height, or reed's own-window anchoring) is undecided and stays out of this task.

## A watch command

`.scratch/hub/watch.sh <slug>` (one watcher per run) becomes a lyx command, or a part of orch's own watcher.
It wakes the orch session when a run changes to a state that needs it, as a backup to the driver's own message to its parent, which is the primary path.

## One land command

`.scratch/hub/land.sh <slug>` plus the steps after it (pull in the prime, delete the branch on origin, `lyx board prune`) become one lyx command.
Deploy stays operator-triggered, so the command either stops before deploying or deploys only when told.

## Continue the last orch session

After a reboot the operator wants the same conversation back, as `claude --continue` gives, not a fresh session reading a handoff.
Today that takes `lyx orch start --adopt <session-id>`, with the id dug out of `~/.claude/projects/`.
`lyx orch` records its session id and offers `lyx orch start --continue` (or makes it the default for a dead strand) to adopt the last orch session.

## The orch role prompt

The orch's working rules live in one committed role stencil beside the other orch stencils (`contracts/stencils/orch/`), so an orch on any machine works by the same rules; today they sit in one machine's file-memory and in handoffs.
`lyx orch` puts the role into its start prompt and points the one-line resume and adopt prompts at it.
The rules, one section per theme:

- Parent-review: a one-shot fork reads the brief, checks scope against the board entry only, and submits `lyx loom review approve|reject <slug>`; a repeat notice starts no second fork.
- PR-Gate: judge each run against its own board goal and its tests, never widening scope through rejects; fix a small goal defect on the task branch, and put new hardening on the board instead of rejecting.
- Board: read and write it only through `lyx board`; a proposal not yet shaped into a task goes on the board as a tier 3 note at once, never in a local draft file; fewer, larger tasks, since each run costs a full Discussion/Plan/Webster/review cycle; a small finding never becomes its own entry, but folds into an open entry whose work overlaps (same files, same context), or into the repo-wide conventions task when it overlaps nothing.
- Bugs in lyx go to GitHub issues; design, features and hardening go on the board.
- Act and fix without asking; ask the operator only about what to build.
- Give `cd <pair> && lyx reed attach` for every run in every status report.

The matching file-memory entries on the hub machine are deleted when the role lands.

## Done when

- The orch starts, watches and lands runs with lyx commands only, and `.scratch/hub/` is gone.
- A started batten run survives the orch's shell and session ending.
- `lyx orch start --continue` after a reboot resumes the last orch conversation.
- An orch cycle's resumed session knows the procedure from its role prompt, and its handoff carries state only.
- A fresh `lyx orch start` on a machine with no file-memory works by the same rules.

## `lyx board upsert` reads a body from a file (seen 2026-10-03)

`lyx board upsert` takes the whole body inside one JSON argument, so changing one section of an entry means reading the body, splicing it and re-encoding JSON in a shell one-liner, which breaks on quoting (an apostrophe in the text) and pushes the orch into throwaway scripts.
Want: `upsert` accepts the body from a file or stdin (for example `--body-file`), so the orch writes the body with its file tools and sends it unchanged.

entries.title: Parent-review gate: wait bound off the boundary, no mid-turn sends, live smoke
entries.brief: Close the cases the first parent-review gate left open: expiry while the writer is mid-turn, sends into a running turn after restart, poll cost, and one live smoke run
entries.body:
## Goal

The parent-review gate holds its promises in the cases the first version left open: the wait bound fires even when the writer never ends its turn, no gate send lands inside a writer turn after a restart, and a live hand-started hub is proven to receive the notice.

## From the PR #336 review (2026-10-02)

- **Live smoke.** The smoke test uses a stub writer that records the typed line, so the SendMessage hop to a real hand-started parent has never run; run it once live.
- **Wait bound off the boundary.** Expiry is checked only at a writer turn boundary (`internal/shuttleengine/wait.go`, `gateAtBoundary`), so a writer stuck mid-turn (for example on a permission prompt for `lyx loom review delivered` in interactive mode) holds the run until `discussion_timeout_min` instead of `parent_review_wait_min`; expiry needs no send, so evaluate it on every tick.
- **Mid-turn sends after a restart.** `AttachGated` replays events from offset 0, so the first tick treats the writer as idle even mid-turn: a notify-carried prompt or a reject re-prompt can be typed into a running turn, and a consumed reject is let through while the writer is still fixing.
- **Turns the loop cannot see.** A turn started by the parent replying to the writer through SendMessage, or by the operator typing, leaves the loop at a boundary; tell the orch fork not to reply to the writer.
- **Poll cost.** While pending at a boundary every 500 ms tick re-runs `discussionparser.Validate`, three locked JSON reads and a `MkdirAll`; throttle re-evaluation to a few seconds.
- **Way-forward from the prime.** The no-open-request refusal names `lyx loom status <run>`, which cannot address the child from the prime; name `lyx batten status` there.
- **`approve --review` and an empty file.** The refusal spec says it refuses a missing or empty file, the code only a missing one; align them.
- **Entry order.** `shedrecipe` does not require `parent-review` to be the gate list's last entry; a must-pass entry after it would be `not_reached` at a deadline finalize while the review is pending.
- **`delivered` after a verdict** can write `delivery.json` after the discussion commit and leave `_lyx` dirty until the next status commit.
- **Round numbers** grow on every fresh spawn with no reviewer (empty `round-N/`, never committed).
- **Review scope.** The brief says "Do not re-review the design's internal quality", narrower than millhouse's `orch-review`; confirm with the operator.

entries.title: lyx orch runs for days without hand repair
entries.brief: Adopt keeps watchers, permission modes mean what they say, attach keeps the orch window size, large-session adopt is tested, status reads the current session
entries.body:
## Goal

The hub runs under `lyx orch` for days without hand repair: an adopt keeps the hub's watchers, the orch pane keeps its height, permission modes mean what they say, and a long transcript stays cheap to read.

## From the PR #337 review (2026-10-02)

- **Watchers after adopt.** The hub's background shells and Monitors die with the session it exits; `orch-template-adopt.md` does not tell the resumed session they are gone or to re-arm them.
- **Window size on attach.** With `window-size latest`, a `reed attach` from VS Code resizes the orch window to that client (seen on the PR #342 review, after #340's folderOpen fix landed).
- **`permission_mode: prompt`** adds no flag, so the session falls back to the user's `defaultMode` (`auto` here); the template comment and the orchengine doc promise prompts.
- **Smoke bypass check** proves nothing where `~/.claude/settings.json` allows `Bash`; assert the bypass footer or use a tool outside the allow list.
- **Large-session adopt** is untested: startup within `startup_timeout_s` and any resume dialog on a real hub transcript (decision record, open risk 2).
- **Stale context reading.** `ResetForFreshLaunch` keeps `LastContextTokens`, so `status` shows the previous session's reading until the first turn end after an adopt.
- **PID reuse** can refuse an adopt falsely; the registry's `procStart` tells a reused pid apart.
- **Transcript read cost.** `ContextTokens` reads the whole transcript on every idle turn end; read from the end.

## Cycle by compact instead of clear (operator idea, 2026-10-03)

The orch's context cycle uses `/clear` plus a handoff file, which starts a new conversation and may drop a Remote Control link the operator relies on from a phone.
Cycling through `/compact` keeps the same session, so Remote Control and session identity survive.
The operator wants the cycle mode as a config option (`clear` or `compact`), not a fixed switch; weigh what the handoff file gives that a compaction summary does not.


## Reopening the prime's VS Code window (seen 2026-10-03)

- A snap auto-refresh of VS Code (rev 257 → 267 at 12:44) left the old instance running; batten's next `code <pair>` call then started a second instance, which restored the prime as a bare folder without the hub workspace's title and colour, and the operator had to close windows by hand.
- Reopening the prime correctly takes `lyx ide spawn <prime-name>`, whose folderOpen chain (`reed up`, `reed add --unless-name orch`, `reed attach`) reattaches to the orch without starting a second Claude; a plain `code` on the prime gets the stale mill-managed `.vscode/tasks.json` and attaches nothing.
- Want: `lyx ide spawn` with no argument opens the worktree it is run in, so the operator restores the prime with one short command; run from the hub root or any hub directory outside a worktree (today it fails there, and the operator had to cd into the prime), it opens the prime.
- Want: a `lyx ide open [<slug>]` that only launches VS Code and writes nothing: the prime through its existing hub workspace file, a pair through its folder and the `tasks.json` already there. `lyx ide spawn` stays the configuring verb; today it rewrites a driven pair's attach-only chain with the interactive one, whose `reed add claude` can start a second Claude in that pair. The no-argument and hub-root defaults above apply to `open`.

entries.title: Hardener: an autonomous behavior-review campaign that replaces crucible
entries.brief: Parked by the operator: settle the Tenter/Hardener design and build the campaign that runs a live-substrate module in a sandbox until it converges
entries.body:
## Goal

Replace `crucible`, the hand-run review-and-fix loop, with `Hardener`.
Hardener is an on-demand campaign after loom that runs a live-substrate module in a sandbox, reviews its behavior round after round, and fixes what it finds until the gates are green.
Then retire `crucible/`, which still writes to `_mill/` and runs its rounds through hand-spawned `crucible-reviewer-<effort>` agents.

## Starting point

- `manifest/designs/hardener.md` (DRAFT): `Tenter` is the round loop on `Treadle`, and `Hardener` is `Shed` wrapping `Tenter` with its own Preflight.
  Rounds respawn every time instead of keeping a persistent thread, and a `progress-judge` runs before and after each round.
- `crucible/README.md` is the method Hardener automates.

## Open before Discussion

- What the handoff must carry losslessly besides the finding-recurrence ledger.
- Where the line falls between the Go scaffolding and the LLM's orchestrator role.
- Whether the round agent reuses the `burler` package or only its prompt template.
- How much of the sandbox provisioning lyx automates.

## Done when

- `lyx` can start a Hardener campaign against a module and run it unattended to convergence or a round cap.
- `crucible/` is deleted, and the design's durable content lives in package docs.

## Notes

- One of the Someday items on `manifest-retire`'s triage list (`hardener`). Landing this entry removes it from that list.

entries.title: Test suite, part 2: derived guards, decoupled recipe tests, no leaked tmux sockets
entries.brief: One invariant-scan harness; registry and CLI-tree tests derived from the real registries; recipe/plan/stencil tests decoupled from their sources; fixtures clean up tmux sockets
entries.body:
## Goal

Tests derive their expectations from the code they guard instead of keeping hand-written copies of lists owned elsewhere, so adding a module, command, config section, path or recipe row edits no test file; and integration tests leave no tmux sockets behind.
Second half of the test-suite cleanup: it builds on `test-suite-change-amplification`'s `internal/testkit` (the scan harness lives under it).
#326 section 2 needs an operator decision before Discussion closes.

## Work items

Each self-contained with file:line evidence in its issue:
- #326 one invariant-scan harness; derive registry and CLI-tree tests (section 2 needs an operator decision: it changes the CLI/Cobra Invariant help-tree tests).
- #327 decouple recipe, plan and stencil tests from their sources.

## From `test-tmux-socket-leak`: Integration tests leave tmux sockets behind

Tests leak tmux sockets: `/tmp/tmux-1000/` holds hundreds of `lyx-Test…`, `lyx-contract-…` and `lyx-warp-bare-…` sockets left by reed/loom integration tests. Test fixtures should kill their tmux server and remove the socket in `t.Cleanup`.

## Operator directive: CONSTRAINTS.md may change

The operator suspects some `CONSTRAINTS.md` invariants, or the way they are enforced, are what made the test suite grow, and authorizes changing them.
Discussion audits the invariants that bear on this task's tests and, for each one that forces duplicated tests or hand-kept copies (per-package copies of the same scan, per-module test obligations, allowlists that mirror code, the do-not-share-test-helpers decision), proposes a change: restate the rule, move its enforcement to one shared scan, or drop it.
A changed invariant lands in `CONSTRAINTS.md` in the same commit as its tests; an invariant's intent is weakened only where the discussion says so explicitly and why.

## Notes from part 1's invariant audit (its decision D13)

- The per-package `seam_enforcement_test.go` and `leaf_enforcement_test.go` copies share root lookup, walk, allowlist and floor scaffolding: #326's one-harness item, which can host part 1's Testkit scan too (part 1's scan does not assume its own shape is final).
- Tier Purity's and Hermetic Env's per-file allowlist entries whose only reason is resolving the module root through `go env GOMOD` mirror each guard's implementation; one shared root resolver in the harness retires them.
- Hand-kept copies of registries production owns: CLI / Cobra Invariant help-tree tests, Sandbox Suite Coverage, the config-section registry, Cwd Resolution's constructor-anchoring and no-transients path mirrors, Shed Recipe Registry's row mirrors, Agent Name and Stencil Ownership tests.
- Plan fixtures: part 1's parent review moved its proposed `internal/testkit/plankit` here, as #327 section 2's plan-fixture writer; it also covers the glyph-plan and file-tree fixture copies in `loomshed` and `loomcli` that part 1's discussion had found.

## Socket leak: findings and direction (ly:orch, 2026-10-03)

`/tmp/tmux-1000/` held about 1,500 dead socket files (656 `lyx-warp-…`, 415 `lyx-001…`, 115 `lyx-contract-…`, the rest per test name) with no tmux server behind any of them: servers exit, their socket files stay.
About 34 tests already run `kill-server` in `t.Cleanup`, which ends the server but leaves the file; others, likely the fabric tests that boot reed (`lyx-warp-…`), have no cleanup at all.
Direction for Discussion to weigh:
- One shared tmux fixture (under `internal/testkit`) for every test that needs a server: a unique socket, `kill-server` and removal of the socket file in `t.Cleanup`.
- The socket under a short per-test temp directory (`tmux -S <path>`, not `-L <name>`), so it goes with the directory even when a test dies; mind the ~108-byte Unix socket path limit, which long `t.TempDir()` paths can exceed.
- A guard: each tmux-using package's `TestMain` compares the socket directory before and after its tests and fails on a new leftover `lyx-*` socket.

entries.title: A batchifier that groups small related cards into one Webster batch
entries.brief: Only the identity batchifier exists; a mechanical batchifier groups cards from their Create/Edit/Uses fields once cards name members as glyphs
entries.body:
## Why

`internal/batcher` has a registry but only the `identity` batchifier, so every card is its own Webster batch.
On `test-suite-change-amplification` (45 cards, 2026-10-03) each batch carried a fixed overhead besides the fork's own work: `record-batch`, `begin-batch`, three short Merriam turns and the fork's start-up, about 16–18 s per batch after quarry v0.2.1 (over a minute before it, #345), plus a fork prompt and Merriam polling per batch.
Many cards there take 40–120 s of work, so for them the overhead is a large share.

## Want

A mechanical batchifier (operator): it groups cards from the plan's own card fields (`Create`, `Edit`, `Uses`, renames), never from an LLM's judgment, selected through `batcher.yaml`'s `active` key, the identity batchifier staying the default.
Cards whose fields show no dependency on each other and no shared target can share a fork; a card that `Uses` another's `Create` follows it.

## Waits on `plan-glyph-precision`

Plans list file paths, not member glyphs, so card fields today only support file-level grouping, which is too coarse to be the point.
The batchifier is built once cards name the members they touch.

## Trade-offs to settle

- A larger batch gives the fork a larger context and makes a failure harder to localize to one card.
- The per-batch validation and drift check (`begin-batch`, `record-batch`) then runs per group, not per card; the operator wants plan drift caught as it happens.
- It should fit the parallel-execution direction in `manifest/designs/webster-parallel-execution.md`, where the same DAG decides which groups may run concurrently.
